subject: Economics
subcategory: Economic Crises That Shook the World
title: The Dot-Com Bust: When the Internet Bubble Burst
description: One-minute skill: The Dot-Com Bust: When the Internet Bubble Burst.

hook.text: Pets.com raised $82 million in its IPO, selling dog food online at a loss. It went bankrupt in 268 days.

buildup.text: The Dot-Com Bust sets up the incentives, the tradeoffs, and the market logic.

discovery.text: The Dot-Com Bust reveals the mechanism connecting incentives to outcomes.

twist.text: The NASDAQ fell 78% by 2002. But companies that survived — Amazon, Google, eBay — became the most valuable in history.

climax.text: The dot-com bubble proved the technology was real but the valuations were fantasy.

punchline.text: The internet changed everything. That didn't make every internet company viable.

quiz.question: What was the lasting impact of the dot-com bust?
options: Overvalued companies died but survivors like Amazon became the most valuable companies ever
